nahhas-irab:1-1.t: الر تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ: the implied structure is "This: those are the verses of the Book."

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: كَذلِكَ نَسْلُكُهُ: the kāf is in the position of an accusative, as a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar (verbal noun). People have discussed the pronoun here: it was said that it refers to the denial; it was said: to the Reminder; and it was said that it is like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82], i.e. its punishment.

nahhas-irab:14-15.t:
وَلَوْ فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ باباً مِنَ السَّماءِ فَظَلُّوا فِيهِ يَعْرُجُونَ (14): and the dialect of Hudhayl is يعرجون. «[Translator's note: the differing vowel (يَعْرِجون) is not marked in the source.]» Regarding the pronoun there are two views: one is that the implied structure is "and the angels continued [ascending]"; the other is that the implied structure is: "Even if We opened to these obstinate disbelievers a gate from the sky and made them enter it so that they ascended to the sky, so that this would be a sign confirming you, they would reject what they saw with their own eyes and say: our eyes have only been dazzled and we have been bewitched, so that we see the thing other than as it is." One says سكر and, by way of intensification, سكّر, i.e. his mind was covered over; and from it was said:
(سكران) "drunk", and it is derived from (السّكر).

nahhas-irab:17-18.t:
وَحَفِظْناها مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطانٍ رَجِيمٍ إِلَّا مَنِ اسْتَرَقَ السَّمْعَ.
مِنْ [i.e. مَنْ] is in the position of an accusative. Al-Akhfash said: an exception outside [the kind of the first]. Abū Isḥāq said: it is permissible for «من» to be in the position of a genitive, the implied structure being "except from whoever eavesdrops" (إلا ممّن استرق السمع).

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: وَالْأَرْضَ مَدَدْناها: by an implied verb.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
رُبَما: there are eight variants of it. Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read رُبَّما with a doubled consonant, and the people of Medina and ʿĀṣim read رُبَما without doubling. The original is the doubled form; the Arabs lighten what is doubled but do not double what is light. Sībawayh said: if you named a man (رب) without doubling and then formed its diminutive, you would restore it to its original and say (ربيب). Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq said: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī related to us from his father, from al-Aṣmaʿī, who said: I heard Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read «ربما» both without doubling and with doubling. He said: the light form is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, and the doubled form the dialect of Tamīm, Qays and Bakr. Abū Zayd related that one says ربّتما and ربتما, this being on the basis of making the word feminine. So these are four dialectal forms. And Abū Ḥātim related: ربما, ربّما, ربتما and ربّتما. «[Translator's note: the vowelling that distinguishes these forms is not marked in the source; they are given as printed.]»
It has no grammatical position according to most grammarians, because (ما) is a restraining particle (kāffa) brought in because (ربّ) is not followed by a verb; so when you bring in (ما), a verb follows it, according to Sībawayh, and nothing else, except in poetry, where a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) follow it. And he recited: [ṭawīl] 257-
صددت فأطولت الصّدود وقلّما ... وصال على طول الصّدود يدوم
(You turned away and made the turning away long; and seldom does union endure through long turning away.)
And the good [usage] is his saying:
258-
وطال ما وطال ما وطالما ... سقى بكفّ خالد وأطعما
(And long, and long, and long has he given drink and food with the hand of Khālid.)
What we have related is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that this is permissible in prose and poetry, just as (إنما) may be followed by a verb or by a mubtadaʾ and khabar. And I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd say: there is no parallel to (ربّ) among the genitive-governing particles, because the way of the genitive particles is that what precedes them is related through them to what follows them, while the way of (ربّ) is that the verb which follows it is related to what precedes it. Al-Akhfash claimed that it is permissible for «ما» to be in the position of a genitive, as an indefinite noun, i.e. "many a thing" or "many a wish". One says: وددت أنّ ذلك كان ("I wished that that had been") when you desired it, [maṣdar] ودّا only; and وددت الرجل when you loved him, [maṣdar] ودّا with ḍamma on the wāw, and مودّة, ودادة and ودادا.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
Al-Farrāʾ said: «من» is in the position of an accusative, and the meaning is "and We made for you in it means of livelihood, and slave-women and slaves". He said: and it is permissible for «من» to be in the position of a genitive, i.e. "and for those for whom you are not providers". The second view is, according to the Basrans, a grammatical error (laḥn), because it conjoins an overt noun to a genitive pronoun. Abū Isḥāq has a third view on it, good and unusual: he said «من» is conjoined to the interpretation of (لكم), and the meaning is:
"We gave you livelihood", i.e. We provided for you, and We provided for those for whom you are not providers.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَإِنْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا عِنْدَنا خَزائِنُهُ: that is, We own it and have power over it; and it was said: by it is meant the rain.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
وَأَرْسَلْنَا الرِّياحَ لَواقِحَ: we have mentioned it [before]. Ṭalḥa, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read وأرسلنا الريح لواقح, and according to Abū Ḥātim this is a grammatical error (laḥn), because (الريح) is singular and so is not described by a plural.
Abū Ḥātim said: it is ugly to say الريح لواقح. He said: as for their saying "the false oath leaves the abode (الدار) desolate wastes (بلاقع)", by (الدار) they only mean the land, as He, Mighty and Exalted, said: فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دارِهِمْ جاثِمِينَ [al-Aʿrāf: 78]. Abū Jaʿfar said: what Abū Ḥātim said about this being ugly is a clear mistake. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: وَالْمَلَكُ عَلى أَرْجائِها [al-Ḥāqqa: 17], meaning the angels, and there is no disagreement among the people of knowledge about that; and likewise (الريح) in the sense of (الرياح). Sībawayh said: "As for the verb, it is patterns taken from the expression of the events of the nouns." And al-Farrāʾ related, in the like of this: "the wind (الريح) came from every place", meaning the winds.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: إِنَّهُ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ: Wise in His governing, Knowing of it.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: We have mentioned it [before]. Among the best of what has been said about it is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him; he said: «مسنون» means "on the path", its implied sense being "on the course (sanan) of the path", its sanan and its sunan; and when it is so, it becomes fetid and changes, because it is water standing apart. «[Translator's note: the source repeats «وسننها» twice, presumably for two vowellings (sanan / sunan) that are not marked.]»

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
It is related from al-Ḥasan that he read والجانّ خلقنه with a hamza [i.e. الجأن], as though he disliked the meeting of two quiescent letters.
The better is without a hamza, and the meeting of two quiescent letters is not objected to when the first is a letter of prolongation and softness and the second is assimilated (mudgham). وَالْجَانَّ is accusative by an implied verb.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: And His saying ساجِدِينَ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: ذَرْهُمْ: it is in the form of a command carrying the sense of threat. One does not say (وذر) nor (واذر); the reason for this according to Sībawayh is that they made do without it by (ترك), and according to others it is the heaviness of the wāw, so that when they found an alternative to it they abandoned it. يَأْكُلُوا is the apodosis (jawāb) of the command; وَيَتَمَتَّعُوا is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: The view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is that it is a tawkīd (emphasis) after a tawkīd. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: (أجمعون) conveys that they were not scattered. Abū Isḥāq said: this is wrong; if it were as he said, it would be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ: Abū Isḥāq said: an exception not of the same kind as the first; he follows the view of those who said that Iblīs is not one of the angels and never was one of them. This is a sound view, indicated by the fact that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has informed us that He created the jinn from fire, and the angels were not created from fire.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: ما لَكَ أَلَّا تَكُونَ: [أَلَّا تَكُونَ] is in the position of an accusative.

nahhas-irab:37-38.t: It is not a granting to him of what he asked; rather it is by way of disdain for him, since he would not reach the misguiding of anyone except one who would not prosper even if he had not whispered to him.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t:
قالَ رَبِّ بِما أَغْوَيْتَنِي: there are several views about it. Among the best of them is that the meaning is "because You have disappointed me of Paradise". One says غوى when one is disappointed (خاب), and أغواه: he disappointed him; and from it: [ṭawīl] 259-
ومن يغو لا يعدم على الغيّ لائما
(And whoever fails/strays will not lack someone to blame him for his straying.)

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: In the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); and outside the Quran it is permissible to omit the wāw. By this He indicated that everyone destroyed or killed is so by his appointed term.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: إِلَّا عِبادَكَ: accusative as an exception (istithnāʾ).

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
قالَ هذا صِراطٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ: [مُسْتَقِيمٌ is] its naʿt (adjective). Ziyād ibn Abī Maryam said:
«عليّ» means (إليّ) "to Me"; he holds that the meaning is the same. It was said: it carries a sense of threat, i.e. to Me is its return and upon its way. And it was said: upon [Me is] its explanation, i.e. the guarantee of that.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t:
إِنَّ عِبادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطانٌ: the original of (ليس) according to Sībawayh is (ليس) [i.e. لَيِسَ]. Sībawayh said:
"As for (ليس), it is made quiescent from the like of (صيد) [i.e. صَيِدَ], just as they said علم ذاك [i.e. عَلْمَ for عَلِمَ]." «[Translator's note: the vowelling that distinguishes the forms is not marked in the source.]» Abū Jaʿfar said: according to the principles of Arabic it should have been said (لاس), since the yāʾ is vowelled and what precedes it is vowelled. Sībawayh said: so they made its weakening the removal of the vowel, because no imperfect, no active participle, no maṣdar and no derivation is formed from it, and it occurs frequently in their speech, so they did not treat it like its sisters — meaning those that operate as it operates. He said: so they treated it like (ليت). Abū Isḥāq said: (ليس) is not conjugated because the future, the present and the past are negated with it, so it had no need of conjugation. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd say: since it resembles «ما», it was prevented from conjugation.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: وَنَزَعْنا ما فِي صُدُورِهِمْ مِنْ غِلٍّ: al-Kisāʾī said: غلّ يغلّ from rancour, غلّ يغلّ from embezzlement (al-ghulūl), and أغلّ يغلّ from treachery. «[Translator's note: the vowelling distinguishing these forms is not marked in the source.]» Others said: the meaning of وَنَزَعْنا ما فِي صُدُورِهِمْ مِنْ غِلٍّ is: We removed from them ignorance, anger and desire for what is not proper, until mutual envy disappeared. إِخْواناً is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: The implied structure is "about the companions of Ibrāhīm's guest (ضيف)", and for this reason (ضيوف) was not pluralized.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: قالُوا لا تَوْجَلْ: whoever says (تأجل) substitutes an alif for the wāw because it is lighter; and whoever says (تيجل) substitutes a yāʾ for it because it is lighter than the wāw; and the dialect of Banū Tamīm is (تيجل) [with kasra on the tāʾ], to indicate that it is from (فعل) [i.e. فَعِلَ]. And one says فلان ييجل, with kasra on the yāʾ; this is anomalous because kasra on the yāʾ is considered heavy, but this was done so that the wāw would turn into a yāʾ.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t:
فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ is the reading of most people. Nāfiʿ read it with kasra on the nūn. It is related that Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the kasra on the nūn is a grammatical error (laḥn); he holds that one does not say أنتم تقوموا, dropping the nūn of inflection. Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh and al-Khalīl allowed the like of this. Sībawayh said: some of those who are trusted read قالَ أَتُحاجُّونِّي [al-Anʿām: 80] and فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ «[Translator's note: printed with fatḥa; Nāfiʿ's reading under discussion is with kasra (تُبَشِّرُونِ).]», and it is the reading of the people of Medina. The original according to Sībawayh is "فبم تبشّرون" with the nūn assimilated into the nūn; then the assimilation was felt heavy, so one of the two nūns was dropped. He did not drop the nūn of inflection, as Abū ʿAmr interpreted; he only dropped the additional nūn. And Sībawayh recited: [wāfir] 260-
تراه كالثّغام يعلّ مسكا ... يسوء الفاليات إذا فليني
(You see it [the hair] like the white thaghām plant, perfumed again and again with musk; it grieves the women who search it for lice when they search me.)
And another said: [wāfir] 261-
أبالموت الّذي لا بدّ أنّي ... ملاق لا أباك تخوّفيني
(Is it with death — which I must inevitably meet, you fatherless one — that you frighten me?)

nahhas-irab:55-56.t:
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read قالُوا بَشَّرْناكَ بِالْحَقِّ فَلا تَكُنْ مِنَ الْقانِطِينَ, and read وَمَنْ يَقْنِطُ, and read مِنْ بَعْدِ ما قَنِطُوا [al-Shūrā: 28], all with kasra. Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read قال ومن يقنط with kasra on the nūn, and «قنطوا» with fatḥa on the nūn. The people of the two Sanctuaries, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read قالَ وَمَنْ يَقْنَطُ with fatḥa on the nūn, and they read «قنطوا» with fatḥa on the nūn. Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī read قال ومن يقنط with ḍamma on the nūn. «[Translator's note: so in the source. The report that the readers of the two Sanctuaries, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read يَقْنَطُ with fatḥa is as printed; the familiar transmission has يَقْنِطُ for them. The vowelling of the bare forms is not marked in the source.]»
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām chose the reading of Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī in this, and claimed that it is more correct in Arabic, and he rejected the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza, because according to him it is on the pattern faʿala yafʿalu; likewise he rejected قنط يقنط. If the matter were as he said, both readings would be errors (laḥn), and this is something not known to occur: that the people of the two Sanctuaries should agree on something and it then be an error — especially as ʿĀṣim is with them, with his eminence, his standing, his knowledge and his place in the language. The two readings he rejected are permissible and good, and their interpretation is contrary to what he said. One says قنط يقنط, and قنط قنوطا, so he is قانط; and قنط يقنط قنطا, so he is قنط and قانط. So if one reads «ومن يقنط», it is according to the dialect of those who say قنط يقنط; and if one reads «ومن يقنط», it is according to the dialect of those who say قنط يقنط like ضرب يضرب; and if one reads يقنطوا, it is according to the dialect of those who say قنط يقنط like حذر يحذر; so he may use both dialects. Abū ʿUbayd narrowed what is broad in the language. And the meaning of ومن يقنط is "who despairs".

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: قالَ فَما خَطْبُكُمْ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:58-59.t: إِلَّا آلَ لُوطٍ ...: Abū Isḥāq said: an exception not of the same kind as the first. إِنَّا لَمُنَجُّوهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t:
إِلَّا امْرَأَتَهُ: he said: an exception from the hāʾ and mīm [of لَمُنَجُّوهُمْ]. Abū Yūsuf interpreted this as an exception referred back onto an exception, and this is the view of Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām: قالُوا إِنَّا أُرْسِلْنا إِلى قَوْمٍ مُجْرِمِينَ إِلَّا آلَ لُوطٍ — so He excepted them from the criminals — "except his wife", so He excepted her from Lot's people, and she came to be with the criminals. He said: just as you say: "He is owed ten by me except four except one", so it becomes seven, because you excepted one from the four and it came to be with the six, making seven. Abū ʿUbayd said: just as you say, if a man says to his wife: "You are divorced three times except two except one", then he has divorced twice. Abū Jaʿfar said: what Abū Yūsuf said is as he said according to the people of Arabic; but what Abū ʿUbayd said is not permissible according to the skilled among the people of Arabic. They say that one does not except half of a thing, nor more than half, and none of the Arabs speaks thus. Exception according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is [akin to] emphasis (tawkīd), «[Translator's note: the source has a stray closing bracket before «التوكيد».]» because when you say "the people came to me", it is possible that some of them remained; then when you say:
"all of them", you have encompassed them. Likewise when you say "the people came to me", it is possible that Zayd was included among them; then when you say "except Zayd", you have made clear, just as you made clear by emphasis. And the meaning of your saying "He has ten with me except one" is "he has with me ten, incomplete"; and it is not permissible to say of five or less than that "ten, incomplete". قَدَّرْنا إِنَّها: ʿĀṣim read قَدَّرْنا [as printed], and the doubling conveys intensification, i.e. We wrote that, informed of it, and knew that she is among those who remain behind (al-ghābirīn). «[Translator's note: the source prints «قَدَّرْنا» with shadda in both places; the contrast drawn with the doubled form implies that ʿĀṣim's reading is meant without doubling (قَدَرْنا).]» We have mentioned it [before].
Among the best of what has been said about it is that the meaning of (الغابرين) is those who remain behind, staying back from going out with him, from their saying غبر when one remains. And so said the people of Arabic regarding the meaning of وَلا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنْكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ [Hūd: 81]: that the meaning is "so travel by night with your family, except your wife". And among the best of what has been said about the meaning of وَلا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنْكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ is that the meaning is:
"let no one turn to what he left behind, but let him go out". And it was said: it is from turning (al-iltifāt), i.e. let there not be from you a going out such that one turns [back].
قالُوا بَلْ جِئْناكَ بِما كانُوا فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ (63): that is, with the punishment about which they were in doubt.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ: from (أسرى); and whoever joins [the hamza, reading فَاسْرِ] makes it from (سرى). Two well-known dialectal forms. «[Translator's note: the source prints «سرّى» with shadda; translated by the evident sense (سرى).]»

nahhas-irab:66-66.t:
وَقَضَيْنا إِلَيْهِ ذلِكَ الْأَمْرَ أَنَّ دابِرَ هؤُلاءِ مَقْطُوعٌ: al-Akhfash said: «أنّ» is in the position of an accusative as a badal (substitute) from (الأمر). Al-Farrāʾ said: it is in the position of an accusative by the dropping of the preposition (accusative by removal of the preposition), i.e. "We decreed to him that matter with this". He said: and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is وقلنا إن دبر هؤلاء, so if a reader read accordingly with kasra on (إنّ), it would be permissible. مُصْبِحِينَ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the implied structure according to al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayd is "when they are entering the morning". Abū ʿUbayd said: just as you say: "You riding are better than you walking". He said:
And I heard an eloquent Bedouin of Banū Kilāb say: "I, as a friend to you, am better than I, as an enemy to you."

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: In the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: قالَ إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ ضَيْفِي: it is singular because it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun): ضفته ضيفا, i.e. I stayed with him as a guest; the implied structure is "people of my hospitality". Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning [of the following] is "Did we not forbid you from hosting all people?" And others said: the meaning is "Did we not forbid you from granting anyone protection against us and keeping us from him?"

nahhas-irab:72-72.t: لَعَمْرُكَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, because oaths are a domain of omission; the implied form is "By your life, [is] my oath". إِنَّهُمْ is with kasra because it is the answer of the oath, and a group of grammarians allowed it with fatḥa. لَفِي سَكْرَتِهِمْ: that is, their ignorance, likened to drunkenness.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: Accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (أشرقوا): they came upon the sunrise, i.e. its rising.

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: That is, exhortations against sins and disbelief for those who draw inferences.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t: وَإِنْ كانَ أَصْحابُ الْأَيْكَةِ: there is no disagreement about declining this one and the one in «Qāf» fully. They disagreed about the one in «al-Shuʿarāʾ» and the one in «Ṣād»: the people of Medina read both without full declension, while the people of Basra and Kufa read them like those two; and this is the truth, because there is no difference among them and the story is one; this is merely like the repetition of stories in the Quran. As for the saying of whoever said that (أيكة) is the name of the town and «الأيكة» the name of the country, it is neither known nor well established. As for the argument of whoever argued from the written text (al-sawād) and said, "I do not decline fully the two in «al-Shuʿarāʾ» and «Ṣād» because in the script they are without an alif", he has no proof in that; this is only according to the dialect of those who say جاءني صاحب زيد لسود, meaning (الأسود): the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the lām, so the lām became vowelled, and the connecting alif fell away because of its being vowelled, and the hamza fell away when its vowel was cast onto what precedes it; and likewise (ليكة).

nahhas-irab:79-79.t: وَإِنَّهُما لَبِإِمامٍ مُبِينٍ: there are two views about its meaning. One is that the imām is the Book which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wrote, because it is before all the books; and the other is that it is the road, because it is followed (yuʾtammu bihi).

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: ما نُنَزِّلُ الْمَلائِكَةَ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ: the original is (تتنزّل), and one of the two tāʾs was dropped for lightness. «[Translator's note: the source has a stray closing bracket after the quotation; the remark about (تتنزّل) refers to the reading ما تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلائِكَةُ, not to the نُنَزِّلُ printed here.]»

nahhas-irab:80-80.t: It was said: the companions of al-Ḥijr are the people of Ṣāliḥ.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: Al-Ḥasan read وَكانُوا يَنْحِتُونَ because it contains one of the guttural letters; and the kasra is more eloquent. «[Translator's note: so printed, with kasra; the explanation (a guttural letter) and the remark that kasra is more eloquent imply that al-Ḥasan's reading is meant with fatḥa (يَنْحَتُونَ).]»

nahhas-irab:87-88.t: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْناكَ سَبْعاً مِنَ الْمَثانِي وَالْقُرْآنَ الْعَظِيمَ: in the hadith, the Quran here is al-Ḥamd [i.e. al-Fātiḥa], because part of the Quran is Quran. لا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلى ما مَتَّعْنا بِهِ أَزْواجاً مِنْهُمْ: do not covet their blessings, and do not grieve over them, i.e. over My blessing upon them. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning of وَاخْفِضْ جَناحَكَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ is: soften your wing towards whoever believes in you and follows you.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: The original of إِنَّا is (إنّنا). نَحْنُ is in the position of an accusative as an emphasis (tawkīd) of [the pronoun governed by] (إنّ); it is permissible for it to be in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); and it is permissible for it to have no position, being a separating pronoun (fāṣila). وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ: the first lām is a genitive-governing lām and the second is a lām of emphasis; no differentiation was needed with the pronoun because the marking differs.

nahhas-irab:90-91.t: كَما أَنْزَلْنا: the kāf is in the position of an accusative, i.e. «And say: I am indeed the clear warner» of a punishment or chastisement like what We sent down upon the dividers. الَّذِينَ جَعَلُوا الْقُرْآنَ عِضِينَ: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā holds that «عضين» is from عضّيت, i.e. I divided, and it is derived from (العضو) "limb"; what is omitted according to him is a wāw, and the diminutive according to him is (عضيّة). Al-Kisāʾī holds that it is from عضهت الرجل, i.e. I accused the man falsely, and the diminutive according to him is (عضيهة). Al-Farrāʾ said: (العضون) in the speech of the Arabs is sorcery. According to the Basrans it is pluralized with wāw and nūn only as compensation for what was dropped from it; and according to the Kufans it ought to have been pluralized on the pattern (فعول), so they sought the wāw that is in (فعول) and brought it, saying (عضون). Al-Farrāʾ said: some of the Arabs say عضينك, making it with yāʾ in every case and inflecting the nūn, as you say مضت سنينك ("your years have passed"); this is common among Asad, Tamīm and ʿĀmir. The reason for it according to him is that since the wāw occurred in the place of a defective letter, they imagined it was the wāw of (فعول), so they inflected what follows it and changed it into a yāʾ, just as some Arabs said with the tāʾ — he related it from Abū al-Jarrāḥ: سمعت لغاتهم ("I heard their dialects", with the tāʾ inflected). But you do not say that with (الصّالحات), nor with what has had its beginning dropped, such as (لدّات).

nahhas-irab:92-92.t: An emphasis (tawkīd) of the hāʾ and mīm.

nahhas-irab:94-94.t:
Abū Isḥāq said: فَاصْدَعْ بِما تُؤْمَرُ, i.e. make it plain and manifest it; derived from (الصّديع), which is the dawn; and a crack (الصّدع) in glass is when parts of it separate from one another. بِما تُؤْمَرُ: [ما with the verb] is a maṣdar according to the Basrans, i.e. "with Our command". Al-Kisāʾī said: the implied structure is "with what you are commanded with (به)", like أَلا إِنَّ عاداً كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ [Hūd: 60], i.e. "in their Lord", and then the bāʾ was dropped. «[Translator's note: the source prints «هود: 6»; the verse is Hūd 60.]» Abū Jaʿfar said: dropping the bāʾ is not permissible according to the Basrans, neither in prose nor in poetry. The Kufans recited, by Jarīr: [wāfir] 262-
تمرّون الدّيار ولم تعوجوا ... كلامكم عليّ إذا حرام
(You pass the abodes and do not turn aside; speaking to you is then forbidden to me.)
And I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: I heard ʿUmāra ibn ʿAqīl ibn Bilāl ibn Jarīr recite it for his grandfather as:
مررتم بالدّيار ولم تعوجوا
(You passed by the abodes and did not turn aside.)

nahhas-irab:96-96.t: الَّذِينَ يَجْعَلُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ: in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (المستهزئين). And the meaning of وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ [al-Ḥijr: 94] is: from answering them when they meet you with ugliness.

nahhas-irab:99-99.t: حَتَّى يَأْتِيَكَ الْيَقِينُ: [يَأْتِيَكَ is] accusative by (حتّى), and its nominative is not permissible because it is future. (اليقين) is death, because every rational person is certain of it.
